missedEssential.fact: The install script scripts/install.sh installs a fresh copy or replaces an older one, then opens the app, selected with --app=studio.
PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MySQL and SQLite use a Grid default view, an SQL console, and support writes.
ClickHouse uses a Grid view and SQL console but supports insert-only writes.
Redis uses a key/value view with Redis commands console, writes only string keys, but can delete keys of any type.
The data grid is virtualized in both directions with page sizes from 10 to 10k and count-all only on request.
Column masking (PII) offers six masks and is display-only; the data itself is never changed.
Kira Studio uses three-tier caching with no speculative prefetch, documented in docs/PERF.md.
Revealing a saved password requires Touch ID or system password confirmation.
The optional local Database MCP server lets an AI client read databases under user-set rules, is off by default, and is enabled from Settings → Database MCP.
MCP prompt mode waits for the user to approve the exact statement.
Building from source requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon with Xcode command-line tools.
Building requires Go 1.27+ and the Wails v3 CLI (wails3), whose version is pinned in go.mod and installed by bun run setup.
Bun is the package manager, script runner and test runner, used for build tooling only; nothing ships a Node runtime.
bun run screenshots must be run by hand and never beside a UI test run because it rebuilds both frontend/dist directories.
Screenshot output must be byte-identical: running it twice must pass git diff --exit-code -- screenshots/.
Go real-engine test cases need Docker and skip without it.
bun run test:claude:studio is opt-in, needs an authenticated claude CLI and spends a few cents of tokens.
Not shipped: light mode, Windows and Linux, DDL editing, exporting results to CSV/JSON files, connection folders, split editor groups, SSH tunneling, code signing and notarization.

missedEssential.fact: Session.Close sends SIGHUP to -shellPID, and bash forwards SIGHUP to its jobs and then exits.
creack/pty v1.1.24 ioctl.go:9 calls f.Fd() for every ioctl, including StartWithSize -> Setsize and the app's own Resize -> pty.Setsize.
os.File.Fd() switches the fd to blocking mode and removes it from the netpoller, so a blocked read(2) survives ptmx.Close() and Go defers the real close until the read returns.
With SHELL=/bin/sh and an escaped child, Close took 6.004s, logged 'session did not exit after SIGKILL and ptmx close', and done stayed false.
Because of RC2, every Close caller, including app-quit CloseAll and window close, pays the full 6s per stuck session.
Under SHELL=/bin/sh, TestSessionCloseKillsProcessGroup fails deterministically (3/3) because the child survives Close in its own process group.

Fixing the design gap means signalling every process group in the session, which changes semantics a real terminal emulator has, such as Terminal.app not killing a dash background job or disowned bash job.
After the fix, with SHELL=/bin/sh the test still fails because the child is alive (the deferred design gap), but there is no WARN, Close takes ~4s, and done closes, on Linux only.

missedEssential.fact: P169 addresses `gh` REST responses over 4 MiB being reported as unreadable, originating from P168 Part 14 finding F16.
The old post-hoc stdout slice did not bound memory, because it only discarded bytes after they were already held.
The size estimates in P169 are arithmetic, not measurement, because no authenticated `gh` was available and the sandbox blocked direct GitHub API calls.
`errors.go` adds const `reasonUnreadable = "GitHub returned an unreadable response"`.

`tooLargeReason()` returns "GitHub's response was over %d MiB, too large to read" using `maxStdoutBytes>>20`, and is a func rather than a const so a test that lowers the cap still gets a true message.
In `api.go`, `get` has no logic change and uses `reasonUnreadable`, which now means only non-JSON from an untruncated body.
`graphql` is restructured so that when the envelope does not decode it runs `classify` first, returning any non-OK status (including too large) as before.
If a measured real page exceeds a few tens of MiB or nears 10 s, a named follow-up phase (GraphQL-projected snapshot) is to be opened in `SPEC.md`, as that is a design change.
P169 was implemented as planned with no deviations, and the size measurement remains an open item in ARCHITECTURE.md.

missedEssential.fact: P257 removes per-file and per-commit added/removed line counts in the git module from the UI because the user found them noisy and useless.
P257 stops `git ... --numstat` spawns whose only purpose was the line counts.
A git 2.43 probe on a conflicted working tree showed `git diff --name-status -M -C HEAD` and `--numstat` list the same path set.

`packages/git-ui/src/components/FileTree.vue` has 4 count render sites: tree-mode and flat-mode directory rows (`N files +x -y`, aggregated in `fileTreeModel.ts`) and tree-mode and flat-mode file rows (`+a -d`, hidden when `isBinary`).
The only `isBinary` consumers are FileTree (to hide counts) and ADE `fileDelta`.
The diff view decides binary at diff time from the diff itself (`porcelain.BodyBinary`, git-core `model/diff.ts` `kind: 'binary'`), covered by flow subtest `binary diff is not text`.

Numstat spawns in `gitsession` `queries.go fileChanges` (CommitDetail), `stash.go StashShow`, `working.go WorkingDetail`, `incremental.go` RangeFiles and `queuefacts.go` (ADE branch files) served counts plus isBinary and are dropped.
D1 rejected keeping a numstat spawn only for binary because it pays a full content diff for an unused flag.
D3: `ParseNameStatusRecords` returns `[]FileChange` directly, setting OriginalPath when non-empty and Similarity for renamed/copied using the same rules as `CombineFileChanges`.
`ade/board_facts.go toWireFiles` builds `adewire.FileChange{Path}`, and `adewire/wire.go` `FileChange` loses `Added`, `Deleted` and `Binary`.
FileTree.vue keeps `N files`, status letter, rename display and tips, while removing the 4 count sites and the `countFormat` import.
`fileTreeModel.ts` drops `additions`/`deletions` from the directory node and aggregation but keeps `fileCount`.
`AdeChangesTab.vue` removes `fileDelta` and its span, and the `justify-between` row becomes a plain truncating path.
Only the `git-graph-detail-visual-linux.png` visual baseline is re-recorded; the other four git-module visual snapshots must pass unchanged because the stash dialog has no file tree.
